newsitem.title: USA: U.S. industrial output soars in November.
newsitem.headline: U.S. industrial output soars in November.

text.p: A rebound in auto production sent U.S. industrial output soaring at its strongest rate in nine months during November, the Federal Reserve said Monday.

Total output increased 0.9 percent last month, the biggest monthly increase since a 1.3 percent jump last February. It followed a 0.2 percent drop in output in October, when many U.S. auto plants were closed because of parts shortages that resulted from strikes against General Motors plants in Canada.
"A rebound in the production of motor vehicles at strike-affected General Motors plants and in the production of related parts and materials accounted for about half of the gain," the Fed said.
Production also was higher for both mining and utilities companies.
The Fed said unusually cold weather in November boosted demand for utilities and added about 0.2 percent to the overall monthly increase in industrial output.
Production by utilities companies increased 2.5 percent last month after a slim 0.3 percent rise in October. Mining output was up 0.1 percent in November following a 0.6 percent drop in October.
There was a striking pickup in auto-vehicle assembly rates after a relatively slack October.

New cars were churned out at a rate of 6.3 million a year in November, compared with 5.5 million in October, while production of popular light trucks increased to 5.6 million a year from 5.4 million in October.
Largely as a result of the auto-industry rebound, manufacturing output grew 0.8 percent in November after contracting 0.2 percent in October.
The Fed noted that there also was a substantial increase in production of commercial aircraft in November and a moderate rise in output of computers and other information processing equipment.
